The GU Congress Atlas.

A structured reading of the official 179-page ESMO 2026 programme: oncology trials, disease tracks, programme collisions and critical questions to take into the room. Primary emphasis: bladder, kidney, prostate, penile and germ-cell malignancies.

01 / Strategic overview

Where the clinical signal is likely to be

Programme-based triage, not an assessment of results that have not been examined.
● P1 · Don't missP2 · Strong interestP3 · Selective
Main conclusion

Protect the original trial presentations, not just the GU-labelled halls.

The critical circuit runs through Friday's perioperative MIBC trials, Saturday's GU proffered papers and Presidential Symposium, Sunday's two RCC sessions, and the Monday cross-disciplinary biomarker and specialty meetings. The single most consequential trap is assuming that the presence of a phase III or LBA abstract implies a positive or practice-changing outcome.

Hard conflict

Friday, 23 Oct · 13:30–15:00

Bladder proffered papers and prostate/penile/germ-cell rapid oral occupy exactly the same window. Saturday 10:15–11:45 also splits the prostate plenary and renal/urothelial rapid oral tracks. See the clash explorer.

Bladder & UTUC

Perioperative therapy collision

KEYNOTE-866, perioperative nivolumab, VOLGA, KEYNOTE-B15 ctDNA and KEYNOTE-905 subgroup data. Distinguish randomized survival endpoints, pathological endpoints and exploratory subgroup analyses.

Kidney & RCC

HIF-2α, adjuvant therapy, rare histologies

LITESPARK-012/011, KEYNOTE-564 long-term follow-up, papillary RCC randomised data, KIM-1 monitoring, CAIX PET and early cellular therapeutics. Compare sequencing and actual comparator standards.

Prostate, penile & GCT

Survival, intensification and emerging biology

PEACE-1 long-term OS, CAPItello-281 updated OS, PROTEUS substudy, Presidential radiotherapy/ARPI data, ctDNA/HRR analytical pitfalls, CLDN6 ADCs and miR-371.

Interpretation boundary. This is an analytical map of the programme, not a results review: titles establish what is scheduled, not efficacy, statistical significance, regulatory status or treatment recommendations. Critical questions are our hypotheses for appraisal, not reported findings. A GU programme listing may coexist with a separate abstract/poster database.
